classes.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on the upper leaf surface, leaf puckering, premature leaf drop, and corky scabs on fruit.
classes.treatment: Apply protective fungicides such as captan, mancozeb, or myclobutanil at bud break; prune canopies to maximize sunlight and airflow; apply sulfur sprays for organic orchards.
classes.prevention: Rake and compost or burn fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering ascospores; select scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Enterprise, Liberty, GoldRush); space trees adequately.

classes.symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots with purple margins and tan centers; firm, concentric dark rings on expanding fruit; cankers on twigs and limbs.
classes.treatment: Prune out dead wood, fire blight cankers, and mummified fruits; apply thiophanate-methyl or captan during petal fall and cover sprays.
classes.prevention: Maintain tree vigor with balanced soil nutrition; avoid mechanical wounding during cultivation; eliminate dead brush and wild host trees nearby.

classes.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and develop raised orange cushions; tube-like structures (aecia) on leaf undersides shedding powdery spores.
classes.treatment: Spray sterol inhibitor fungicides (e.g., immunox / myclobutanil) starting at pink bud stage through petal fall.
classes.prevention: Remove nearby Eastern Red Cedar (Juniperus virginiana) trees within a 1-2 mile radius if feasible; plant resistant varieties like McIntosh or Red Delicious.

classes.symptoms: Vibrant, uniformly green foliage with no chlorosis, necrotic spotting, or pathogen lesions.
classes.treatment: No disease intervention needed. Maintain routine irrigation and seasonal nutritional schedule.
classes.prevention: Perform regular scouting, seasonal dormant oil sprays, and maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization.

classes.symptoms: Smooth, firm, uniformly green leaves with healthy vascular development.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain acidic soil conditions (pH 4.5 - 5.5).
classes.prevention: Apply pine bark or peat moss mulch, maintain uniform drip irrigation, and avoid over-fertilizing with nitrates.

classes.symptoms: White to grayish powdery fungal patches on young leaves and fruit stems, upward leaf curling, stunted shoot growth.
classes.treatment: Apply potassium bicarbonate, sulfur, or quinoxyfen at petal fall; remove heavily infected water sprouts.
classes.prevention: Prune canopies to increase air circulation and reduce high relative humidity within foliage; avoid excess nitrogen applications.

classes.symptoms: Healthy deep green leaves with crisp margins and normal photosynthetic vitality.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard orchard maintenance.
classes.prevention: Regular canopy pruning, monitoring for aphids and borers, and routine spring copper sprays.

classes.symptoms: Small necrotic spots with yellow halos expanding into long, narrow, rectangular gray-to-tan lesions restricted by leaf veins.
classes.treatment: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin) when lesions reach the third leaf below the tassel.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant corn hybrids; practice 1-2 year crop rotation with soybeans; till crop residue to accelerate decomposition of overwintering fungi.

classes.symptoms: Oval to elongated cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, erupting with powdery spores.
classes.treatment: Apply foliar fungicides such as propiconazole or pyraclostrobin if rust pustules appear before silking on susceptible hybrids.
classes.prevention: Select resistant corn hybrids; plant early in the season to evade peak windborne spore showers.

classes.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or cigar-shaped lesions (1-6 inches long) that mature into dark, olive-black sporulating centers.
classes.treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin-based fungicides at early VT-R1 growth stages if threshold conditions are reached.
classes.prevention: Utilize hybrids with Ht-resistance genes; rotate fields with non-host crops; manage residue through tillage where appropriate.

classes.symptoms: Broad, robust, dark-green leaves showing crisp parallel venation and vigorous vegetative growth.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain scheduled nitrogen sidedressing and moisture management.
classes.prevention: Maintain balanced soil pH and optimal plant population density.

classes.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular leaf spots with black fruiting bodies (pycnidia); berries shrivel into hard, black, wrinkled mummies.
classes.treatment: Apply myclobutanil, kresoxim-methyl, or mancozeb from pre-bloom through early fruit set; prune mummified clusters.
classes.prevention: Maintain canopy training systems that promote airflow; dispose of overwintered cane cankers and mummies.

classes.cause: Phaemoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium aleophilum (fungal complex)
classes.symptoms: Tiger-stripe interveinal leaf chlorosis and necrosis; small dark spots on berry skins; internal wood decay in trunks.
classes.treatment: No direct cure once vine vascular system is infected; surgically renew trunks or prune affected cordons below necrotic zones.
classes.prevention: Protect pruning wounds with wound sealants or biocontrol agents (Trichoderma); prune during dry weather late in the dormant season.

classes.symptoms: Irregular dark reddish-brown to black spots on leaves, becoming dry and brittle, leading to premature leaf drop and sunburnt bunches.
classes.treatment: Apply copper oxychloride, bordeaux mixture, or systemic carbendazim sprays at onset of symptoms.
classes.prevention: Prune excess vine canopies; improve drainage; ensure thorough post-harvest debris removal.

classes.symptoms: Lush palmate green leaves without chlorosis, necrotic patches, or fungal sporulation.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain standard vineyard nutrition and trellising.
classes.prevention: Routine preventive sulfur sprays against powdery mildew and adequate canopy shoot positioning.

classes.cause: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (bacterium transmitted by Asian Citrus Psyllid)
classes.symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle leaf chlorosis, yellow shoots, vein corking, lopsided bitter fruit that stays green at the bottom.
classes.treatment: No known chemical cure once infected. Apply foliar nutritional sprays to extend productivity; remove infected trees to protect surrounding groves.
classes.prevention: Rigorous insecticidal control of Asian Citrus Psyllid vector (Diaphorina citri); use certified disease-free nursery stock; install protective screen enclosures.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked angular purple-black lesions on leaves that drop out creating a shot-hole appearance; pitted, cracked fruit spots.
classes.treatment: Apply oxytetracycline or low-dose copper bactericides during shuck-split through petal fall; avoid excessive nitrogen.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant varieties (e.g., Candor, Bounty); establish windbreaks to reduce windblown sand abrasion that opens infection ports.

classes.symptoms: Bright lanceolate green foliage free of necrotic lesions, gummosis, or shot-hole defects.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard stone-fruit orchard protocol.
classes.prevention: Dormant copper sprays against leaf curl; regular thinning and pruning.

classes.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, circular to irregular lesions on foliage turning brownish-black with yellow halos; defoliation leading to fruit sunscald.
classes.treatment: Apply fixed copper bactericides combined with mancozeb for improved efficacy; use streptomycin sprays in seedling flats if permitted.
classes.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; rotate with non-solanaceous crops for a minimum of 2 years.

classes.symptoms: Glossy, uniform deep green leaves and stout, well-branched vegetative architecture.
classes.treatment: No disease intervention required. Ensure adequate calcium and magnesium supply.
classes.prevention: Maintain drip irrigation to avoid blossom end rot; scout regularly for thrips and aphids.

classes.symptoms: Brown to black concentric target-ring spots on older bottom leaves; leaves turn yellow and drop; dry leathery rot on tubers.
classes.treatment: Apply protectant fungicides (chlorothalonil, mancozeb) or systemic strobilurins (azoxystrobin) at first lesion detection.
classes.prevention: Maintain plant vigor through balanced nitrogen; practice 3-year crop rotation; avoid overhead irrigation late in the afternoon.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips, white velvety sporulation on leaf undersides in humid conditions; rapid vine collapse and foul-smelling tuber rot.
classes.treatment: Immediately apply systemic fungicides (mefenoxam, cymoxanil, cyazofamid); destroy infected foliage prior to harvest.
classes.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers; monitor blight forecast tracking; destroy cull piles and volunteer potato plants.

classes.symptoms: Vigorous composite leaves displaying rich green coloration with no chlorotic spots or mildew fuzz.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain scheduled hilling and moisture regimes.
classes.prevention: Regular preventative fungicide scheduling during cool wet weather; insect control against Colorado potato beetles.

classes.symptoms: Serrated, pinnately compound leaves showing clean venation and robust cane development.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain organic mulch and drip watering.
classes.prevention: Prune spent floricanes after harvest; ensure good row spacing for drying winds.

classes.symptoms: Uniform trifoliate emerald foliage without mosaic, rust pustules, or target lesions.
classes.treatment: No treatment required. Monitor for weed pressure and root nodule nodulation.
classes.prevention: Crop rotation with corn; use fungicide-treated high-germination seed.

classes.symptoms: Talcum-powder-like white fungal colonies on upper and lower leaf surfaces, petioles, and stems; leaves turn yellow, brown, and brittle.
classes.treatment: Spray horticultural oils, potassium bicarbonate, or fungicides containing myclobutanil or trifloxystrobin at first sign.
classes.prevention: Select resistant squash cultivars; provide generous plant spacing; utilize drip irrigation to avoid wet foliage.

classes.symptoms: Small, irregular purple-to-brown spots on upper leaf surfaces that coalesce, making leaves look scorched and burnt; brown calyx lobes.
classes.treatment: Apply captan, copper hydroxide, or thiophanate-methyl early in spring as new growth starts.
classes.prevention: Remove dead and infected leaves during spring cleanup; maintain weed-free beds; rotate strawberry plantings every 3-4 years.

classes.symptoms: Glossy, trifoliate serrated green leaves showing robust crowns and clean runners.
classes.treatment: No disease treatment required. Continue standard runner management and straw mulching.
classes.prevention: Ensure good soil drainage to prevent crown rot; scout for spider mites and slugs.

classes.symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked dark spots on leaves, becoming dry and brown; rough, scabby spots with white halos on green fruit.
classes.treatment: Spray fixed copper mixed with mancozeb; apply bacteriophage biocontrols during early evening hours.
classes.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds; sanitize stakes and cages with bleach solution; avoid handling wet plants.

classes.symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings resembling a target board, surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos on lower foliage; collar rot on seedlings.
classes.treatment: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper fungicides; prune bottom 12 inches of leaves; apply bacillus subtilis for bio-management.
classes.prevention: Rotate crops away from tomatoes/potatoes for 3 years; stake plants; lay plastic or straw mulch to halt soil-to-leaf rain splashing.

classes.symptoms: Large, irregular, water-soaked pale green or brown lesions on leaves; white fluffy mold growth on underside in damp conditions; dark, greasy fruit rot.
classes.treatment: Immediately apply systemic fungicides (mandipropamid, cyazofamid, dimethomorph); bag and discard severely infected plants.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant); destroy volunteer tomato plants; ensure rapid canopy drying.

classes.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces matching olive-green or velvety brown spore growth on the underside; progressive curling and wilting.
classes.treatment: Apply copper fungicides or chlorothalonil; improve greenhouse exhaust ventilation and lower humidity below 85%.
classes.prevention: Select resistant greenhouse cultivars; increase plant spacing; avoid overhead sprinkler watering.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1/8 inch) with grayish-white centers and dark brown margins; tiny black speck pycnidia in center of lesions.
classes.treatment: Apply protectant fungicides like chlorothalonil or copper oxychloride; remove lower infected leaves promptly.
classes.prevention: Mulch soil surface to prevent spore splash; stake and prune foliage; eliminate solanaceous weeds such as nightshade.

classes.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling on upper leaf surfaces; bronze leaf discoloration; delicate silky webbing on undersides and growing tips.
classes.treatment: Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil, or sulfur (do not mix oil and sulfur); release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
classes.prevention: Keep plants well hydrated in hot weather; spray water underneath leaves to disrupt webs; control surrounding dusty weeds.

classes.symptoms: Pinpoint brown lesions on foliage that enlarge into circular necrotic spots with light brown centers and faint target-like concentric rings.
classes.treatment: Apply azoxystrobin, difenoconazole, or boscalid fungicides upon early detection; clear infected crop debris.
classes.prevention: Enhance row spacing for airflow; avoid overhead irrigation; practice balanced crop rotations.

classes.cause: Begomovirus (transmitted by Silverleaf Whitefly, Bemisia tabaci)
classes.symptoms: Severe upward leaf cupping, reduced leaf size, chlorosis along leaf margins, bushy stunted growth, and massive flower drop.
classes.treatment: No cure for viral infections once contracted. Remove and bag infected plants immediately to prevent whiteflies spreading virus to neighbors.
classes.prevention: Install 50-mesh insect screens in greenhouses; deploy yellow sticky cards; apply systemic insecticides (imidacloprid) for whitefly control; plant TYLCV-resistant varieties.

classes.symptoms: Mottled dark and light green mosaic leaf patterns, leaf distortion ('shoestringing'), fern-like leaves, internal brown fruit wall browning.
classes.treatment: No chemical virucide available. Promptly rogue out infected plants; sanitize hands and pruning shear blades in nonfat dry milk (20%) or trisodium phosphate.
classes.prevention: Use certified virus-free seed; plant resistant cultivars (marked Tm-2a); prohibit smoking/tobacco handling before working with plants.

classes.symptoms: Lush, fragrant composite leaves with rich green chlorophyll coloration, sturdy stems, and unblemished foliage.
classes.treatment: No disease treatment required. Continue balanced potassium and calcium fertilization.
classes.prevention: Ensure consistent soil moisture to prevent blossom end rot; regular scouting and clean trellising.
